description: Get any test run (standard/param/mission/compliance) by id, including per-step results: outcome, transcript, similarity scores, words. Use when you need per-step breakdowns OR when you do not know if the run is mission or standard. For mission-specific shape (verdict, evidence, judgeReasoning) prefer getMissionTestRun. For listing across runs use listTestRuns; for counts use aggregateTestRuns. Returns 404 cross-workspace.
name: getRunResults

callDurationSecs.description:
Real call duration in seconds (post-answer → last node), surfaced from
`callMetadata.callDurationSecs`. Preferred over the wall-clock diff
(`completedAt − startedAt`), which inflates by 100–150s+ from queue wait,
container start, ringing and post-call stashing. Same field billing meters on.
Rows with no tester duration (mission runs) report the container's
computed call length here instead.

callTelemetry.description:
Call-level telemetry captured during an IVR test call, nested onto
`TestRun.callTelemetry`. Populated for standard, mission and compliance
runs by the tester / mission-tester containers.
nopaque's own carrier cost is internal and is never returned.

coverage.description: Fraction of the call containing speech (0–1).

backgroundNoise.description:
Standard tests: the background-noise bed the call played (see `BackgroundNoise`).
Absent when no noise was configured.

backgroundNoiseError.description:
Standard tests: why the background-noise bed failed to start. The call still ran,
without noise. Absent when the bed started or no noise was configured.

quality.description: Voice-quality metrics (MOS, jitter, packet loss) per direction.

streamingFailures.description: Times our audio stream to the call failed to connect (a test-platform fault, not the system under test).

answerToFirstUtteranceMs.description: Time-to-first-response — answer to first utterance, in milliseconds.

dialToAnswerMs.description: Ring latency — dial to answer, in milliseconds.

turns.description: Per-turn telemetry breakdown for turn-based containers.

items.description:
Per-step / per-turn telemetry. Nested onto `TestStepResult.turnTelemetry`
(per-step containers) and `CallTelemetry.turns[]` (turn-based containers
such as mission-tester / voice-agent).

hold.description:
Emitted on `hold` step results. `endedBy` is `elapsed` (the full hold was served) or
`call_ended` (the far end hung up first); it is a plain string, not an enum, so a future
container value cannot fail strict client validation.

llmExtraction.description: LLM extraction telemetry — model, token counts, latency and hallucination flag.

responseLatencyMs.description: Per-turn response latency (bot/IVR turn-around) in milliseconds.

carrier.description:
Bring-your-own-carrier (invite-only): the carrier route this run was dialled through,
recorded when the run was dispatched. It still names that route after the config's
`carrierRouteId` is changed or removed. Absent when the run was dialled normally. See
`GET /testing/carrier-integrations` for the route's name and settings.

carrierDetail.description:
Telnyx's record of this call, fetched once a few minutes after the call ends and stored
on the run (absent until then). `status` is `not_found` when Telnyx had no record after
three tries. Give `sipCallId` to your carrier or SBC team to find this exact call in
their logs.

destination.description: The number dialled, from a carrier lookup (refreshed every 90 days).

numberType.description: e.g. uan (UK non-geographic), fixed line, mobile, voip.

hangupDetails.description: Who ended the call at the SIP level: send_bye (us) or recv_bye (the far end).

retriedInternally.description: The network re-routed the call before it connected (adds to dial-to-answer time).

shakenStir.description: STIR/SHAKEN attestation of the caller ID: A, B or C.

sipInviteFailureStatus.description: SIP status when the call never connected (e.g. 486, 503).

carrierEvents.description:
What the carrier's event log and the call recording say about this call, derived once a
few minutes after the call ends and stored on the run (absent until then). Times named
`...Secs` are seconds after the call was answered. `status` is `not_found` when the carrier
had no events for the call after three tries, `error` when they could not be read. A source
that could not be read is named in `errors`; the others are still filled.

dial.description: Where the carrier was told to send the call's events and audio (host, port and path only).

failedWebhooks.description: Carrier events about this call that could not be delivered to the test platform.

playbacks.description: Each audio clip we asked the carrier to play, in order.

status.description: How the playback ended, e.g. completed. Absent when no end was reported.

recording.description:
Answer timing measured on the two-channel call recording (the system under test on one
channel, us on the other). Seconds from the start of the recording, which starts at answer.

ivrFirstAudioSecs.description: When the system under test first made sound.

ivrSegments.description: Speech from the system under test, as [start, end] pairs in seconds.

status.description: stereo: measured. mono: one side of the recording was lost. missing / none: no recording.

turns.description: One per stretch of our audio.

answerGapSecs.description: ourOnsetSecs minus ivrPromptEndSecs. About 1 s is normal.

ivrPromptEndSecs.description: End of the last prompt that had finished before we started.

ivrSpeakingSinceSecs.description: Present when the system under test was already speaking when we started: when it began.

streaming.description: The media stream to the test platform starting, stopping or failing.

failurePattern.description:
Load-test calls that did not pass: why the call failed, as a named pattern with an owner and
the values that put it there (`evidence`). Absent on passed calls, and on calls not yet
classified. `rulesVersion` says which version of the rules produced it.

lateStart.description:
Load-test calls: true when the system under test first spoke later after answer than the
test's late-answer threshold (6 s by default), on passed and failed calls alike. Absent
when nothing measured it.

originalOutcome.description:
Passed with note: the call's outcome before a `verdictNote` changed it to `PASS`. Absent
unless a note changed the outcome.

outcome.description: Unified run outcome — see MissionTestRun.outcome. Optional/nullable for historical rows pre-backfill.

verdictNote.description:
Passed with note: why a call (or step) that failed on its hold check counts as passed.
`hold_unconfirmed`: the call reached hold and the line had sound on it, but the live check
could not confirm music (set by the tester, `by: live`). `hold_music_rechecked`: after the
run, the hold detector heard music in the call's recording (`by: recheck`). `outcome` is
`PASS` and `originalOutcome` keeps the outcome before the note. Absent on calls and steps
without a note.

detail.description: One plain sentence, to show as it is.

detector.description: The version of the hold detector that judged it.

stepIndex.description: The step the note is about.

window.description: The part of the recording checked, in seconds after answer (re-check).

config.description:
Scripted regression test plan. A `TestConfig` is a reusable plan of ordered `TestStep`s
that callers re-run against a phone number via `POST /testing/runs`.

allOf.description:
Caller background noise: café chatter, city street traffic, home (children and a
baby crying) or wind buffeting. The level is fixed per sound.

backgroundNoise.description: Caller background noise played under the call. Omit for none.

carrierRouteId.description:
Bring-your-own-carrier (invite-only). Dial this config's calls through one of the
workspace's carrier routes, over the workspace's own SIP trunk, instead of nopaque's
network. Carrier routes are set up with nopaque. A config with a route dials through it
or not at all: if the route cannot be dialled when a run starts, the run is refused and
the number is never called normally. A refused `POST /testing/runs` returns 409 (or 503);
a scheduled run, batch or sweep records a failed run whose `errorMessage` says why; a
load test fails before it starts. Carrier calls are metered as `carrier_testing`
(load tests: `carrier_load_testing`), not `testing`.
Omitted when the config dials normally.

allOf.description:
The transcription language of a STANDARD test or a MAPPING run — the
language the callee is expected to speak, used to transcribe the call.
Absent means `en-GB`: every omit path is unchanged, so an existing
config without the field transcribes as British English exactly as
before. Anything outside this set is rejected with 400.

The English variants lead, then `multi` (code-switching), then the
remaining languages alphabetically by display label. Mirrors
`api/packages/core/transcription/languages.ts` (Zod) — the single
source of truth; a drift test keeps this enum equal to it.

DISTINCT from `CallLanguage`, which is the language a MISSION test
call is held in. The two lists do not overlap cleanly and are not
interchangeable: bare `en` is a valid `CallLanguage` and is INVALID
here (use `en-GB` or `en-US`), and most codes here are not call
languages at all.

language.description:
Transcription language the config's calls are transcribed in.
Resolved to `en-GB` when the config was created without one, so
every config created since the field existed carries a value;
configs saved before it have none, which also means `en-GB`.

lineNoise.description:
Quiet line noise (-60 dBFS) played under every call so the line is never digitally
silent. Absent or `true` means on (the default); `false` turns it off for this config.

maxDurationSecs.description:
Whole-call ceiling in seconds. When omitted the tester applies its own default of 300.
Every `hold` step's `durationSecs` must fit inside it.

allOf.description:
Thresholds and re-prompt phrases that load-test failure patterns use for this IVR. Every
field is optional; an omitted one uses the platform default.

lateAnswerSecs.description:
Seconds from answer to the IVR's first speech above which a call counts as a late start
(and a failure can be "late answer, straight to hold"). Default 6.

repromptPhrases.description:
Phrases that mean the IVR is re-prompting ("did not understand us"). Replace the
defaults: "I didn't get that", "sorry, I didn't catch", "please say".

silentTailSecs.description:
Seconds of silence from the IVR, after our reply and up to hangup, for "silent after our
reply". Default 10.

patternSettings.description:
Load-test failure-pattern thresholds and re-prompt phrases for this IVR. Omit for the
platform defaults.

phoneNumber.description: E.164-formatted phone number the test calls.

profileId.description: Voice / data profile for `standard` configs only. Omitted for `parameterized`.

requiredParameters.description: Required parameter labels for `parameterized` configs only.

scheduleId.description: Schedule that triggers automated runs (use `template:<id>` to create from a built-in template).

allOf.description:
One step within a scripted test config, as sent on create and update. The same fields as
the stored step (`TestStep`), except that `id` may be left out.

One step within a scripted test config. A `dtmf` / `audio` / `listen` step waits for an
expected transcript from the IVR, then optionally sends a DTMF digit or audio response.

A `hold` step is different: it just stays on the line for `durationSecs` (for example
while a call is transferred and hold music plays) and carries ONLY `id`, `name`, `type`,
`durationSecs` and, optionally, `expectMusic`. `expected`, `threshold` and `timeout` do not apply to it and are
absent on a stored hold step.

Per-type requirements: `dtmf` / `audio` / `listen` need `expected` (server defaults:
`threshold` 90, `timeout` 30). `hold` needs `durationSecs`.

acceptAdditionalAnswers.description:
`dtmf` / `audio` / `listen` steps only, optional. When true the step also passes on any
wording in `additionalAnswers` (each scored with its own threshold). Missing or false
means off. Create and update return 400 for a non-boolean. Ignored on other step types.

additionalAnswers.description:
`dtmf` / `audio` / `listen` steps only, optional. Other acceptable wordings of
`expected`, used only when `acceptAdditionalAnswers` is true and kept when it is false.
While on, the step waits up to the longest of its own `timeout` and the answers'
timeouts; a match on any wording ends the wait. At most 10. Create and update return 400
for an invalid entry. Ignored on other step types.

items.description: One other acceptable wording of a step's `expected` prompt.

expected.description: The wording. Must contain non-space text.

threshold.description: Similarity percentage this wording needs. Defaults to the step's `threshold`.

timeout.description:
Seconds this wording may take, counted from the start of the step. Defaults to the
step's `timeout`. It can lengthen the step's wait but never shorten it.

audioUrl.description: Audio URL when `type` is `audio` (manual entry; usually resolved via `profileItemId`).

delay.description:
Optional "send DTMF anyway" timer. If set, the action fires after this many seconds
even if the threshold has not been met. Legacy field; prefer `timeout`.

dtmf.description: DTMF digits to send when `type` is `dtmf` (manual entry; usually resolved via `profileItemId`).

durationSecs.description:
`hold` steps only (required there): seconds to stay on the line. A JSON number, fractions
allowed, greater than 0 and at most 1800. It must also be no longer than the config's
`maxDurationSecs` (300 when that is unset). That ceiling bounds the WHOLE call, not just
the hold, so this is necessary but not sufficient for the hold to complete. Create and
update return 400 for a violation.

expectMusic.description:
`hold` steps only, optional. When true the step fails unless at least half of the hold
was queue music (judged per second from the call audio): use it to prove a transfer
reached a queue. Every hold reports what it heard in its result either way. Stored only
when true. Create and update return 400 for a non-boolean.

expected.description:
Expected transcript (or regex-like phrase) to match before the step succeeds.
Applies to `dtmf` / `audio` / `listen`; absent on `hold` steps.

id.description:
Step identifier. Optional when sending a step: the server generates one when it is
left out. On update, send a step's existing `id` to keep it the same step; a step sent
without one is stored with a new `id`. Always present on a stored step.

isTransfer.description:
Optional, any step type. Marks the script's transfer step, which load-test failure
patterns use to tell "not transferred" from "failed after transfer". When no step is
marked, the first `hold` step with `expectMusic` is the transfer step. Stored only when
true; at most one step may be marked. Create and update return 400 for a non-boolean or
for more than one marked step.

profileItemId.description: Profile item reference. Resolved server-side to the runtime DTMF / audio payload.

replyDelayMs.description:
`audio` steps only (optional): milliseconds to wait after the bot's end of turn before our
clip plays. Omitted means no extra delay. Ignored on other step types.

threshold.description:
Similarity percentage required for the transcript match to succeed. Server default 90
for `dtmf` / `audio` / `listen`; absent on `hold` steps.

timeout.description:
Maximum seconds to wait for the expected match before failing the step. Server default 30
for `dtmf` / `audio` / `listen`; absent on `hold` steps.

type.description:
Step action type — keypad input, audio response, passive listen, wait for an inbound
callback, or hold (stay on the line for `durationSecs`).

id.description: Step identifier. Always present on a stored step.

items.description: A step as stored and returned: a `TestStepInput` that always carries its `id`.

type.description:
`standard` runs the steps as-is; `parameterized` requires `requiredParameters` filled
at run-time (sweep / batch dispatchers supply them).

version.description: Bumped on every update — clients can use for optimistic concurrency.

dtmfMarkers.description:
Standard tests only: when the tester sent DTMF, relative to the start of the
recording. Absent when the run sent no digits (never `null` or empty).

items.description:
One DTMF send on a standard test. `spans` (one per tone) is present only when the
call's audio encoding is G711 (PCMA/PCMU), where tone timing is known.

durationMs.description: Tone duration per digit in milliseconds.

sentAtSec.description: Seconds from the start of the recording when the digits were sent.

items.description: Per-step execution outcome attached to a `TestRun`. Returned by `GET /testing/runs/{id}`.

actionType.description:
One of `dtmf`, `audio`, `listen`, `wait_for_callback` or `hold` if the step took an action.
`hold` results carry `threshold` 0, `expectedTranscript` '' and `similarity` 0, which are
placeholders and not a match score. Outcome PASS means the hold elapsed; FAIL with
`turnTelemetry.hold.endedBy` = `call_ended` means the far end hung up first.

duration.description: Step duration in seconds (or `undefined` if the step did not run).

matchedAnswer.description:
Which wording matched, set on a pass when the step's `acceptAdditionalAnswers` is on:
0 is the step's `expected`, n is `additionalAnswers[n-1]`. Absent otherwise.

originalOutcome.description:
Passed with note: the step's outcome before a `verdictNote` changed it to `PASS`. Absent
unless a note changed the outcome.

turnTelemetry.description:
Per-step / per-turn telemetry. Nested onto `TestStepResult.turnTelemetry`
(per-step containers) and `CallTelemetry.turns[]` (turn-based containers
such as mission-tester / voice-agent).

hold.description:
Emitted on `hold` step results. `endedBy` is `elapsed` (the full hold was served) or
`call_ended` (the far end hung up first); it is a plain string, not an enum, so a future
container value cannot fail strict client validation.

llmExtraction.description: LLM extraction telemetry — model, token counts, latency and hallucination flag.

responseLatencyMs.description: Per-turn response latency (bot/IVR turn-around) in milliseconds.

verdictNote.description:
Passed with note: why a call (or step) that failed on its hold check counts as passed.
`hold_unconfirmed`: the call reached hold and the line had sound on it, but the live check
could not confirm music (set by the tester, `by: live`). `hold_music_rechecked`: after the
run, the hold detector heard music in the call's recording (`by: recheck`). `outcome` is
`PASS` and `originalOutcome` keeps the outcome before the note. Absent on calls and steps
without a note.

detail.description: One plain sentence, to show as it is.

detector.description: The version of the hold detector that judged it.

stepIndex.description: The step the note is about.

window.description: The part of the recording checked, in seconds after answer (re-check).

outputSchema.description:
Response for `GET /testing/runs/{id}` — the `TestRun` row enriched with `stepResults`
and an inline `config` snapshot of the parent `TestConfig`.
